taxonomyNote: Formerly included in Contia tenuis; recognised as a distinct species by Feldman and Hoyer (2010), originally spelled longicaudae; NatureServe gives the corrected spelling longicauda.
fieldMarks: Longer tail than the common sharp-tailed snake, with 43-58 subcaudal scales (C. tenuis has 24-42).
behavior: Active mostly in the rainy season; retreats underground in the dry season and is sometimes found alive on roads at night.
Diet is apparently restricted mainly to slugs; females lay a clutch of up to 9 eggs, probably in June or July.
habitat: Fairly mesic, well-shaded areas, typically mixed evergreen forest dominated by Douglas-fir and redwood, and woodland with mixed conifer and oak canopy.
range: Outer Coast Ranges of northern California and southwestern Oregon, the Klamath Mountains, and parts of the southern Oregon Cascades; parapatric with C. tenuis in places. Not in Canada.

lookalikes.name: Common sharp-tailed snake
lookalikes.howToTell: Shorter tail with fewer subcaudal scales (24-42 versus 43-58).
